text: dsh-highlightpin 是面向 DSH Web 对话界面的原文钉子插件：用户可以划选一条已完成消息中的文本并保存，供上下文压缩后找回。它在输入框上方提供钉住按钮和详情面板，也注册 /hlpin 命令。每枚钉子可设为按需补回、常驻背景或重点约束；插件会在原文离开上下文后补回 pin，并将另外两档放入系统提示词。面板和命令还可查看、删除钉子及字符预算。适合需要跨压缩保留约束、公式或代码片段的 DSH 用户；不需额外 API Key。

dsh-highlightpin lets DSH Web users save selected message text and recall it after context compaction. Manage on-demand, resident, and highlighted pins from the composer dock or /hlpin command. View budgets, inspect or remove pins, and change their level. No API key is needed.

dsh-highlightpin 的功能「划选并保存消息原文」：在已完成的用户或助手消息中划选文本，点击输入框上方的图钉；插件对齐到会话源文本后保存，并标记匹配精度。
dsh-highlightpin 的功能「压缩后补回与常驻提示」：为每枚钉子选择 pin、resident 或 highlight：pin 在原文离开上下文后补回，其他两档进入系统提示词。
dsh-highlightpin 的功能「查看和管理会话钉子」：通过详情面板或 /hlpin 命令查看钉子与字符预算、展示内容、删除钉子或修改保留级别。

dsh-highlightpin README · highlightpin：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin. Select any stretch of text in a conversation — a constraint, a number, a formula, a piece of code — and pin it with one click. From then on, no matter how the context is compacted, what the model receives is that **source text**, not a summary.

dsh-highlightpin README · Three levels：| Level | Behaviour | Good for | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **pin** (default) | Does nothing while the text is still in context; once compaction drops it, the extract text is re-inserted verbatim near the tail before the next request | Most pins | Never touches the system prompt, so it does not break the prefix cache on its own |
| **resident** | Lives in the system prompt with neutral wording: "consult it when relevant; no need to bring it up" | Important background: you want the model to match on it the moment it matters, without you mentioning it every turn | Costs one prefix-cache invalidation when you switch levels |
| **highlight** | Lives in the system prompt with emphatic wording: "follow it when relevant; if it conflicts with your latest explicit instruction, the latest instruction wins" | Constraints and priorities the model must keep honouring | Same as above; emphasis also raises how often the model brings it up on its own |

dsh-highlightpin README · Three levels：`resident` and `highlight` are deliberately two separate levels. "The model can always find it" and "the model always keeps it in mind" are different things, and emphasis has side effects of its own — so the choice is yours.

dsh-highlightpin README · Installation：From npm (published releases):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-highlightpin@0.1.2
```

Or straight from the GitHub source:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add 'https://codeload.github.com/sbearbug/dsh-highlightpin/tar.gz/v0.1.2'
```

On the web profile, replace `desktop` with `web`. After installing or upgrading, **fully quit and restart DSH**, then refresh the page, so that host and client both load the new version. Existing pins survive.

dsh-highlightpin README · Compatible DSH versions：`peerDependencies` declares `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`. The DSH plugin manager checks these peers with `semver.satisfies(runtimeVersion, range, { includePrerelease: true })` and blocks installation and activation on a mismatch.

dsh-highlightpin README · Compatible DSH versions：The range carries an explicit prerelease branch on purpose: under ordinary semver semantics a single `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` does not match the `0.2.0-rc.*` builds, because node-semver admits a prerelease only when some comparator in the range shares its exact `major.minor.patch` tuple and itself carries a prerelease tag.

dsh-highlightpin README · Compatible DSH versions：| DSH version | Status |
|---|---|
| 0.2.0-rc.2 | **Verified live** — development and real-machine checks both ran on this version |
| 0.1.7-rc.1 / 0.1.7-rc.2 | **Offline suite passes**; CI re-runs the same suite against this line on every push |
| Other 0.2.x | Inferred from the APIs used, not verified individually |
| ≤ 0.1.6 | **Unsupported**: `CommandDefinitionId` does not exist at 0.1.5 and below, and the 0.1.6 line's session-event validation already differs |
| ≥ 0.3.0 | Not claimed |

dsh-highlightpin README · Usage：1. Select text inside **one** finished user or assistant message.
2. Click the pin above the composer.
3. Click the arrow beside it to open the details panel: switch each pin between "recall / resident / highlight", check budget usage, or unpin.

dsh-highlightpin README · Usage：When you select inside a formula, the selection is expanded to the whole formula and what gets stored is the TeX source. Select the rendered $\nabla_\theta J(\theta)$ and the plugin stores `$\nabla_\theta J(\theta)$` — not the glyphs on screen. Selections inside code keep their indentation and line breaks.

Everything is also available from the command line:

dsh-highlightpin README · Usage：| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/hlpin list` | List every pin, its level and budget usage |
| `/hlpin last` | Pin the most recent assistant reply in full |
| `/hlpin show <n>` | Show one pin's full text |
| `/hlpin drop <n>` | Unpin |
| `/hlpin level <n> pin\|resident\|highlight` | Change a pin's level |

dsh-highlightpin README · Design notes：- **What is stored is source text, not screen text.** The client serialises the selection first (formulas back to TeX, copy buttons and line numbers stripped out), and the host then locates the matching source substring in the session log. Alignment reports one of three fidelities: `source-exact` (a clean hit), `source-normalized` (matched after whitespace and Markdown normalisation, but still storing a source slice), or `rendered` (no match — it stores the display text and **tells you so**).
- **`pin` only re-inserts after the original is gone.** Right after pinning, the text is already in context, so re-injecting it would be pointless. It comes back only once compaction has shadowed it — and at that moment the prefix cache was already invalidated. So the default level cannot break caching by construction.
- **The decision is a pure function that keeps no ledger.** Every step re-decides from "is this text still in context", and records nothing like "already re-inserted". A rejected step, a plugin restart, or the recall notice itself being compacted later therefore cannot lose a pin.

dsh-highlightpin README · Design notes：The full set of trade-offs is in [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

dsh-highlightpin README · Verification status：- **Live**: "pin → `/compact` → next message" has been run end-to-end in DSH. The shadowed source text appeared in the next request's input, byte-identical to what was stored, with a matching SHA-256. Evidence: [docs/PROBES.md](docs/PROBES.md) and [docs/m1-live-0.1.4.json](docs/m1-live-0.1.4.json).
- **Offline**: alignment, selection serialisation, the decision function, all three injection paths, budgets, routes, commands and React interaction are covered by tests, run by CI on every push.

dsh-highlightpin README · Configuration：| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `maxPinChars` | 16000 | Total source characters across `pin` pins |
| `maxResidentChars` | 6000 | Total source characters across `resident` pins |
| `maxHighlightChars` | 2000 | Total source characters across `highlight` pins |
| `holdSubagents` | `false` | Whether subagent sessions are covered too (off by default, to avoid wasting tokens) |
dsh-highlightpin README · Configuration：Characters are counted in UTF-16 units. Neither the number of pins nor the length of a single pin is capped; only the total per level is.

dsh-highlightpin README · Limitations：- Selections must stay within a single message; cross-message selections are not supported.
- Streaming messages, reasoning content and tool output are not supported.
- Pins belong to one session; forked sessions do not inherit them.
- One writer host per profile is supported.
- "Highlight" here is an emphasis level in the model input; it does not draw a visual highlight on the original message.

dsh-highlightpin README · Development：```sh
npm ci
npm run check   # build the client + run all tests + loader check
npm run eval    # controlled fixture: byte-exact preservation through all three levels
```
